blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Implementing digital supply chain tools is less about software and more about adoption. The best ERP in the world is useless if the team ignores it; the simplest spreadsheet, used well, beats an abandoned system every day of the week. Technology only pays off when the people using it trust it, understand it, and let it change the way they work.

Successful implementations share a few habits. They start small, with one use case that will visibly help the team. They include the users in the design, instead of presenting them with a finished system. They protect the roll-out from unrealistic deadlines. And they measure adoption honestly — who actually uses it? — rather than counting licences issued.

Technology does not save supply chains on its own. People using the right technology, well, do.

items.q: According to the text, what does implementing digital supply chain tools depend on most?
options: Adoption by the people who use it
The size of the IT budget
items.why: "less about software and more about adoption" — o que decide é o uso real pelas pessoas.

items.q: What habits do successful implementations share?
options: They start small, include the users, and protect the roll-out from unrealistic deadlines
They present a finished system to the whole company at once
They count how many licences were issued
They buy the most advanced ERP available
items.why: "They start small… include the users in the design… protect the roll-out from unrealistic deadlines."

items.q: How does the author say adoption should be measured?
options: By the number of licences issued
By the amount spent on software
By who actually uses the tool
By how quickly it was installed
items.why: "measure adoption honestly — who actually uses it? — rather than counting licences issued."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Users should be included in the design
Unrealistic deadlines can damage a roll-out
Buying a powerful ERP is enough to fix a supply chain
A simple spreadsheet used well can beat an abandoned system
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro argumenta que a tecnologia sozinha não resolve — comprar um ERP potente não basta.

items.q: The final line, "People using the right technology, well, do," suggests that…
options: the right tool matters more than the people
results come from people combined with the right tool, used properly
any technology works if the budget is large enough
items.why: Inferência: o crédito vai para as pessoas usando a ferramenta certa, e bem — não para a tecnologia isolada.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily explicando como está resgatando a implementação. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, the ERP roll-out failed last year, and I want to be honest about why. We bought a brilliant system, trained everyone in one weekend, and then went live across all six warehouses at once. Six months later, most people had quietly gone back to their old spreadsheets.

This time I'm doing the opposite. I've picked one small team — just the inbound desk here in the main warehouse — and one use case: tracking incoming shipments. Nothing else. If we can make that one thing genuinely easier for them, we've earned the right to expand.

I'm also protecting the deadline. Last time we promised the board a full launch in three months, which was never realistic, and the pressure pushed us to skip the training. This round, I've told them plainly: give me twelve weeks with one team, and let me prove the value before we scale.

And here's the part that matters most. I'm not going to report how many licences we've handed out. I'm going to report how many people actually log in and use the tool every day. That number is the only one that tells the truth.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why did last year's ERP roll-out fail, according to Emily?
options: The software was too weak for the warehouses
They went live everywhere at once and people returned to old spreadsheets
The team refused all training from the start
The board cancelled the budget halfway through
items.why: "went live across all six warehouses at once… most people had quietly gone back to their old spreadsheets."

items.q: What is Emily doing differently this time?
options: Launching in all warehouses on the same day
Starting with one small team and one use case
items.why: "I've picked one small team… and one use case: tracking incoming shipments. Nothing else."

items.q: Why did the previous team skip the training?
options: The staff already knew the system
The budget did not cover it
Pressure from an unrealistic three-month deadline
items.why: "we promised the board a full launch in three months, which was never realistic, and the pressure pushed us to skip the training."

items.q: What does Emily mean by "we've earned the right to expand"?
options: Expansion is only justified once the small case proves it helps the team
The team must expand before proving anything
Expansion happens on a fixed schedule regardless of results
The board will automatically approve more spending
items.why: Inferência: crescer é consequência de provar valor primeiro, não uma etapa garantida.

items.q: Why does Emily prefer to report daily logins rather than licences handed out?
options: Licences are more expensive than logins
The board asked specifically for login data
Real usage tells the truth about adoption; licences do not
items.why: Inferência: ela quer medir adoção real — quem usa de fato — não números que parecem bons no papel.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The project's success depends on adoption, not installation." Adoption means…
options: people actually taking up and using the tool
the day the system goes live
items.why: Adoption = adoção: quando as pessoas de fato passam a usar a ferramenta.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "An ___ system that nobody logs into is worse than a simple spreadsheet."
items.why: Abandoned = abandonado: sistema largado, sem uso.

items.q: "We chose one use case to prove the value first." A use case is…
options: a specific task the tool is meant to help with
a legal contract for the software
items.why: Use case = caso de uso: uma tarefa concreta que a ferramenta resolve.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Promising a full launch in three months was completely ___."
items.why: Unrealistic = irrealista: prazo impossível de cumprir.

items.q: "The investment only pays off when people use the tool well." To pay off means to…
items.why: To pay off = compensar, dar retorno real.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre implementação de sistemas. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We plan to roll out the tool team by team." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "The board wants the CIO to sign off on the pilot before we scale." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "Several warehouse leads pushed back on the tight deadline." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar de algo.

items.q: "The team agreed to log usage daily but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it out to the end
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Counting licences won't move the needle on real adoption." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível — aqui, no negativo, não faz.
